div.h1: Onboard a whole team in one upload.
div.p: CSV in, activation emails out, cards live. The rollout pattern that scales from 5 people to 5,000.

div.style: background: #EEF2FF; border-left: 3px solid #2D5BFF; padding: 14px 18px; border-radius: 8px; margin-bottom: 28px;

div.div: Who can run this: the /bulk-onboard flow is locked to users with the Vinc Manager role (or Odoo system admins, who inherit it). Grant it from Settings → Users & Companies → Users → Access Rights → Vinc. Regular internal users have no access to the bulk-onboarding models via RPC or UI.
div.p: Bulk onboarding takes a CSV with one row per future card. Two columns are required, the rest are optional:

ul.li: Required: name, email
Profile: phone, mobile, function (job title), about
Address: street, street2, city, zip, country, state
Social: linkedin_url, facebook_url, twitter_url, instagram_url, whatsapp_url, youtube_url, calendly_url
URL: website_slug (auto-generated from name if omitted)

div.p: Unknown columns are ignored, so it's safe to upload a richer HR export and let Vinc pick what it needs.
📥 Download the starter CSV — pre-populated with five example rows, headers, and per-column hints in the first row.
From the user dashboard, click Bulk Onboarding (admin-only button). You'll land on the wizard at /bulk-onboard:

ol.li: Upload CSV — drag-and-drop or pick a file. Vinc parses and previews the first 5 rows.
Review & map — confirm column mappings; fix typos in row data inline.
Set defaults — pick a template, primary/secondary colors, and lead-form behavior to apply to every card. Per-row overrides win.
Submit — Vinc creates the cards in a single transaction and (if enabled) sends activation emails.

div.p: Each cardholder receives an email with their card URL, a magic-link to set up their own credentials in Odoo, and a one-line "what to do next." The activation template is a regular Odoo mail.template — see Email Automations & Digests for editing.
div.div: Activation emails go through your configured outgoing mail server. If your team uses a transactional sender (Postmark, Mailgun, AWS SES), wire it up in Odoo before the bulk upload — sending 200 cards through Gmail SMTP will trip rate limits.
div.p: The submit step validates the entire CSV before writing anything. If a row fails, you get a per-row reason and the upload doesn't half-commit.

ul.li: Duplicate slug — two rows resolved to the same website_slug. Fix one or supply explicit slugs.
Duplicate email within the upload — Vinc dedupes within the file before insert.
Email already belongs to an existing user — the row is flagged so you can decide whether to reassign or skip.
Slug collision with an existing card — pre-existing card has the same slug. Reassign.
Invalid email — failed format validation. Fix or remove.

div.div: There's no hard row limit enforced by the controller, but in practice keep batches under ~500 rows so the activation-email queue doesn't backlog. For larger rollouts, split into multiple uploads and stagger them.

div.h1: From card scan to pipeline-ready opportunity.
div.p: How Vinc-captured leads land in Odoo CRM, who picks them up, and where you tune the rules.
When a visitor submits the lead form on a card, Vinc creates one crm.lead record (Odoo CRM's opportunity model). The mapping:

ul.li: name — derived from the cardholder + visitor (e.g., "Lead from Jane's card — John Smith")
contact_name, email_from, phone — straight from the form
partner_vcard_id — Vinc-specific: links back to the card that captured the lead
tag_ids — the lead tags configured on the card at capture time
type = opportunity
description — the visitor's notes, if your form's notes field is enabled

div.p: Vinc auto-assigns each new opportunity to the card's owner. The resolution order is:

ol.li: Look up a res.users whose login matches the card's email. If found, that user becomes user_id.
Otherwise fall back to the user who created the card record (partner.create_uid), unless that's a system / public user (id ≤ 4).
If neither resolves, the opportunity is left unassigned and Odoo's standard team rules take over.

div.p: For more sophisticated patterns — round-robin across a sales team, geo-based routing, account-based routing — layer Odoo's standard CRM lead-assignment rules on top. They run after Vinc's user_id assignment, so configure them to either trust Vinc's pick or override it explicitly.
div.div: To opt out of Vinc's auto-assign and rely entirely on Odoo's team-based rules, leave the cardholder's email distinct from any Odoo user login. The fallback to create_uid is skipped for system users, so cards created via the public /get-started route by anonymous visitors don't accidentally get assigned to OdooBot.
div.p: Vinc-captured leads behave like any other CRM opportunity. They show up in:

ul.li: The standard pipeline kanban (filterable by Vinc tag)
List, calendar, and graph views
The user dashboard's "Recent Leads" widget (Vinc-only filter)

div.p: The "Vinc-only filter" is a saved search on partner_vcard_id ≠ False — useful for measuring how Vinc compares to your other lead sources.
Lead tags applied at capture time are the single most useful piece of structured data for downstream reporting. Treat them as the spec for your weekly review:

ul.li: Source attribution — which card / channel / event drove this lead
Intent qualification — what the visitor was after
Follow-up triage — who picks this up next

div.p: Educate cardholders on tags during onboarding. Tags applied 30 days later, when context is gone, are noise.
A 10-minute walkthrough that takes a blank NFC card from box to working in someone's hand.

Buy NTAG215-chip cards. They're widely available, hold enough memory for a URL many times over, and work with every modern phone (iOS 13+, Android 4.4+). Skip the cheaper NTAG213 — they're tighter on memory and you'll regret it the first time you want to encode anything richer.

Search "NTAG215 PVC card" on your usual supplier (Amazon, AliExpress, or a regional NFC distributor). Look for matte-finish PVC cards if you want to print on them, or pre-printed blanks if you'll add a sticker. Avoid the keychain fobs — they're awkward to hand to people.
Install NFC Tools on your phone (iOS App Store or Google Play, free). The flow is the same on both platforms:

ol.li: Open NFC Tools, tap Write, then Add a record.
Pick URL / URI. Paste your card's URL (e.g., yoursite.com/jane-doe).
Tap OK, then Write. Hold the card flat against the back of your phone until you hear the confirmation beep.

div.p: Two cards in two minutes once you've done the first. For a team rollout, bring the box of blanks to a single rollout meeting and program them assembly-line.
NFC Tools offers two modes; URL-write is what you want.

ul.li: URL-write (recommended): the card stores your Vinc URL. When tapped, the phone opens the URL. Updates are instant — change the page server-side, every card already in the wild reflects the change on the next tap.

Direct-write (avoid): the card stores the contact data directly as a vCard payload. The phone shows "Save contact?" without opening a page. Sounds smooth, but: no analytics, no lead form, no updates after the card is printed. You're stuck.

div.div: The whole point of Vinc is the live page behind the URL. Direct-write throws that away.
div.p: Before handing the card to a customer, tap-test it on:

ul.li: Your own phone (sanity check)
A different OS (e.g., test on iOS if you wrote with Android, and vice versa)
A locked phone (NFC works on iOS even when locked, on most Androids too)

div.p: If the tap doesn't trigger, 90% of the time the card is just oriented wrong — try moving it slowly across the back of the phone until the chip aligns with the phone's NFC antenna (varies by model).

div.h1: The automation stack, end to end.
div.p: Three flavors of automated email — intro, leadback, and digest. Each has a job; each is editable.

When a lead is captured on a card with intro emails enabled, Vinc fires a one-shot intro email synchronously, immediately after the opportunity is created. No cron, no delay. The template uses Odoo's standard mail-template system, with placeholders for the lead's name, the cardholder's name, phone, email, and the card URL.
Intro emails are opt-in per card (toggle Intro email enabled on the card's form view). When off, leads still land in CRM but no automated reply goes out.
div.div: Because intro emails fire inline with the lead-capture request, your outgoing mail server's responsiveness affects the lead form's response time. If your SMTP host is slow, lead submissions feel slow. Use a transactional sender (Postmark, Mailgun, AWS SES) for sub-second send times.
div.p: Leadback is Vinc's spec for "what happens after the form submission." Two independent tracks per card:

ul.li: Email track (toggle Send email). One automated email back to the lead. Delay preset: immediate, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 1 hour, or custom (any number of minutes / hours / days). Default: immediate.

Messaging track (toggle Enable messaging). Generates a tap-to-message link in one or more of three channels: WhatsApp, Viber, Telegram. Same delay presets as the email track. Default template: friendly & short, with placeholders for {contact_name}, {vcard_url}, {booking_url}, and conditional {if field}…{/if} blocks.

div.p: Leadback is the single highest-leverage feature for converting captured contacts into actual conversations. A common pattern: immediate email + a 5-minute WhatsApp tap-link, both opt-in for the cardholder.
Each cardholder can receive a weekly digest summarizing their card's performance: scans, views, leads captured, top-rated reviews. The digest is opt-in and configurable per user.
For administrators, the org-level digest aggregates across all cards your account manages, with leaderboards by lead count and review count. Useful for sales-team standups.
All the Vinc templates live in Odoo's standard Settings → Technical → Email Templates, prefixed with Vinc — so they cluster alphabetically. Search for Vinc — in the list and you'll see:

ul.li: Vinc — Introduction Email (to new lead) — fires when a lead is captured and intro email is enabled on the card.
Vinc — New Lead Notification (to card owner) — alerts the cardholder when someone submits their form.
Vinc — Digest Email — the weekly/monthly performance summary.
Vinc — Bulk Onboarding Invitation — activation email for bulk-onboarded users.
Vinc — Bulk Onboarding Completion — admin summary after a bulk batch completes.

div.p: They're regular Jinja-style templates with full access to the lead, card, and user records. Customize tone, add brand fields, swap CTAs.
div.div: Editing email templates is permanent across all cards using that template. If you want a per-card variant, duplicate the template first and assign the duplicate on the relevant card's form view.
